data.author: davidlange6

data.title: perf(build): only look for the Python interpreter in DD4hepConfig
data.author: chrisburr
data.body:
I've been looking at speeding up the cmake configuration time in LHCb and I found that `FIND_PACKAGE(Python)` was being called many times. This ends up being slow due to `python-config` being called several time and the build we use of Python has a high startup overhead.

Unless DD4hep was built with Geant4 there is no need to look for the `Development` components.

This ends up saving ~1.5 seconds on the builds I was benchmarking with:

|       | Baseline      | Patched       |
|-------|---------------|---------------|
| Rec   | 18.8 / 16.4 s | 15.1 / 15.2 s |
| Moore | 17.0 / 16.1 s | 14.2 / 14.7 s |


BEGINRELEASENOTES

- DD4hepConfig: look only for the Python interpreter when DD4hep was built without Geant4 (and not the development component)

ENDRELEASENOTES

data.title: Avoid assuming 64-bit unsigned long when decoding versions
data.author: jmcarcell
data.body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES
- Avoid assuming 64-bit unsigned long when decoding versions.

ENDRELEASENOTES

Version decoding does not need to assume that `unsigned long` is 64 bits. Use `UINT64_C(0xFFFF)` masks to extract each 16-bit component and accept `uint64_t` in `decode_version`, matching the encoded version type.

This preserves preprocessor usage and existing behavior on LP64 platforms, without truncating encoded versions where `unsigned long` is 32 bits.

Applies also to EDM4hep.

I couldn't come up with a good solution in the original design so I made Claude build me one using the *builder patt…
